# airrbag

> Reverse proxy for Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Readarr and Whisparr that shows
> where every library file came from (Usenet, public torrent, private
> tracker, direct download, library file) and refuses deletes that would
> break a private-tracker seed (hit-and-run protection). Go, single static
> binary, Apache-2.0.

airrbag answers one question per library file: what happens to the bytes a
torrent is still seeding if this file is deleted? It compares the file's
device and inode with every file of every torrent in qBittorrent,
Transmission, Deluge or rTorrent (or their resume data on disk), applies the
private tracker's minimum seed time and ratio, and returns one of four
verdicts: keep (deleting is a hit-and-run), frees-nothing (hardlink of a
seed), safe, unknown. The *Arr UI gets source badges and a confirmation
dialog; the API gets HTTP 409 for a delete that would end an owed seed.

Use it when: you seed on private trackers, the *Arrs hardlink or import
from the torrent client, and you want deleting from Sonarr/Radarr/Lidarr,
or from tools such as Maintainerr pointed at airrbag, to be safe.

## Facts

- Image: ghcr.io/fishingpvalues/airrbag (distroless, non-root, read-only root filesystem)
- One listener per *Arr instance; open the listener instead of the *Arr's own port
- Config: airrbag.yml with instances, clients, path_mappings, trackers, guard
- Media mounted read-only; airrbag never deletes or moves files itself
- Authentication is delegated to the *Arr (session cookie or API key)
